Hotochin wrote: Harry,

2. The flag limit is sitting on a strong support/resistance line. How would you know not to go long at a flip zone or FTR?

Let me clarify my second question for you. When price engulfed your flag limit that you marked in green, how would you know to not trade at an immediate retest of that zone as a flip area? This would occur in the consolidation area immediately after the break of the flag limit.

Hotochin wrote: Let me clarify my second question for you. When price engulfed your flag limit that you marked in green, how would you know to not trade at an immediate retest of that zone as a flip area? This would occur in the consolidation area immediately after the break of the flag limit.

Thanks,

because if the rise after the FL is consumed, does not go high enough, it often falls back to test the last swing low, in that case it reacted there but went even lower later. this is less probable trade of course but is one of the plays in the flag. this whole scenario of FL engulfed and price dropping is a trap and happens way too often if you look for it. why? because it catches whoever bought at the place you wanted to buy.

now all this is what i asked you guys to go and look for after the flag limits article. find a decent looking flag, price goes to FL, does it break/hold? where price goes next? how important is the last swing that fills the pole/or breaks to the other direction. what price does on return. does it create an FTR there? what areas can you trade safely?

even if you didnt notice this is a flag you can trade it as Pedini and Sunnytrader and others (please forgive me for not mentioning everyone) do so often

i hope it helps
What do you guys think? FTR=First Time Retest

Hi all,

I'm new to RTM and first of all I wanna say that it is really an incredible site, I like everything from the quality of the material to the principle behind the site. So I've been spending the past week studying the material, watching Sam Seiden's webinars, and trying my best to get familiar with everything. Like anyone new to something, I have quite a few questions to ask, and I would like to start off by posting a losing trade which I took yesterday. I really hope to learn from this trade and hope that someone can correct my analysis.

Below is the daily chart of USDCHF. I noticed a significant S/R flip zone around 0.938. Price broke up strongly out of it on 23rd April, and yesterday pulled back to it.

On the hourly chart, I saw price compressing downwards so I took that as a good sign that price was going to break up again. My entry came when price formed a pin bar (blue arrow). I interpreted it as a rejection of the S/R flip level. It was also a FTB to the 1H demand zone (purple rectangle) so I figured weak bulls were shaken out, breakout shorts were trapped, and the buy orders at the demand zone were filled. I went long with my stop below the pin and was stopped out just now.

Could anyone point out any flaw in my analysis? Would greatly appreciate it! Oh and I'm not too sure where posts like this should go, so do direct me to the right thread if this is not it.:)

Tan,

I would say that sometimes its ok to post questions like these in this thread for class participation. For attention to a particular item like RBR or key levels, those should be kept in the homework thread with that specific name or your journal. Otherwise this thread becomes more of an advisory service than a learning forum. Of course having said that, I can understand that sometimes its hard to get a response in the homework thread. I don't want to speak for IF, but I am assuming this thread is mainly for trades that are up for discussion with full details on entry, not just a specific swap line or pivot. Thats just my guess though.

I am speaking from experience because I have posted questions in here myself and with so many new traders asking very specific questions, by the time someone experienced comes in here many of the questions are old. In the homework folders we are concentrating on one specific item, this makes the conversation flow much better.

Having said that I don't want to comment on your chart yet as I am newer as well. I don't want to confuse you. My only comment would be that I don't know if I would go long there on your H1. You are trying to go long when price just closed below a key level on the daily and after an engulf! I would think you should be looking for shorts, not longs.
